title: Institutional Regeneration Framework
legal_character: Voluntary advisory and implementation-support framework; not a source of charter authority, member-state consent, employment power, funding entitlement, adjudication, emergency command, programme closure, or institutional dissolution.
non_authority_clause: Audit is not jurisdiction. Participation is not consent. A reform proposal is not charter change. A completed workshop is not regeneration. A successful pilot is not permission to scale. Conformance is not legitimacy or success.
action_class_assignment_basis: Primary action classes are implementation mappings derived from §4 domains and each record title and purpose; they do not narrow secondary functions or GMEAIA crosswalks.

reform_classes.definition: changes current behavior while the main selection pressures remain;
improves resources, skills, infrastructure, or operational ability under the current mandate;
changes rewards, penalties, funding, promotion, appointment, exposure, or accountability;
changes who may decide, block, inspect, fund, or compel;
changes the conditions that cause the institution's characteristic behavior to return after leadership, policy, or pilot changes.

consequence_profiles.name: Exploratory and non-consequential
consequence_profiles.examples: public education, optional brainstorming, non-operative drafting, simulation, or demonstration.
consequence_profiles.core: one compact non-operative record identifying the method or artifact, responsible actor, authority effect, and non-activation status. Data and closure semantics are added where material.

consequence_profiles.name: Voluntary bounded practice
consequence_profiles.core: actor and method; voluntary scope; consent, refusal, and withdrawal; implementation responsibility; stop and expiry; complaint and correction route.

consequence_profiles.name: Operational or consequential action
consequence_profiles.core: constituting authority; affected parties; causal responsibility; authorization and activation; implementation ownership and dependencies; monitoring and review; challenge and remedy; closure and unresolved-duty custody.

consequence_profiles.name: Protected-domain or constitutional action
consequence_profiles.core: `CP2` plus `GMEAIA-56` or `GMEAIA-57` and the controlling specialized interface. Ordinary GMEAIA conformance is never sufficient by itself.

records.title: Framework adoption, consequence profile, and institutional scope
records.purpose: Records whether the institution is exploring, piloting, adopting internally, or referencing the framework; selects CP0–CP3 without implying charter change or success.

records.title: Constituting instrument and mandate baseline
records.purpose: Pins the institution’s charter, treaty, statute, resolutions, delegations, presently valid mandate, and authority-formation type.

records.title: Member, governing-body, amendment, and response-authority map
records.purpose: Identifies who may amend the charter, budget, representation, programmes, offices, or dissolution provisions and who owes a response to consequential referrals.

records.title: Stakeholder, beneficiary, worker, and affected-outsider map
records.purpose: Identifies member states, staff, unions, contractors, beneficiaries, affected communities, partners, and affected outsiders.

records.title: Affected Indigenous nation and protected-knowledge record
records.purpose: Records the specific affected nation, its representatives, law, consent, non-engagement, and protected-knowledge requirements.

records.title: Purpose, mandate, and objective-reproduction audit proposal
records.purpose: Defines the audit question, scope, consequence profile, authority effect, evidence, causal and selection-pressure questions, reviewers, exclusions, and use restrictions.

records.title: Mandate evidence, provenance, access, and correction register
records.purpose: Separates charter text, performance evidence, stakeholder testimony, political claims, model outputs, access refusals, uncertainty, and corrections.

records.title: Purpose clarification and deliberation process
records.purpose: Records a facilitated dialogue, participants, affected standing, dissent, limitations, and advisory conclusions.

records.title: Mission relevance, reform class, causal responsibility, and option analysis
records.purpose: Compares symptom, capacity, incentive, authority, reproductive, transfer, merger, closure, and dissolution options without deciding among them.

records.title: Reform pacing, response-time, capacity, and impossible-mandate assessment
records.purpose: Advises sequencing, clocks, support needs, causal constraints, and whether the mandate or pilot is presently possible.

records.title: Power, capture, common-mode, and objective-reproduction map
records.purpose: Maps influence, funding, appointment, prestige, informal authority, retaliation, shared infrastructure, professional dependence, and continuation incentives.

records.title: Evolution Cell charter, independence, and terminal condition
records.purpose: Defines appointment, mandate, term, access, budget, limits, dependency-reduction, complaints, removal, succession, and closure.

records.title: Evolution Cell proposal, agenda, causal theory, and handoffs
records.purpose: Records a bounded reform proposal, reform class, causal mechanism, responsibilities, clocks, dependencies, and terminal condition.

records.title: Staff, union, and workplace consultation
records.purpose: Records labour consultation, bargaining duties, occupational effects, dissent, retaliation safeguards, and remedies.

records.title: Beneficiary and service-user consultation
records.purpose: Records access needs, dependency, service-continuity risks, representation, affected standing, and challenge.

records.title: Governance blueprint and authority-effect classification
records.purpose: Classifies youth, citizen, Indigenous, future-generation, advisory, voting, or veto templates as options requiring lawful constitution.

records.title: Constituency and representation design
records.purpose: Defines who is represented, selection, mandate, conflicts, accountability, removal, internal plurality, and affected non-parties.

records.title: Charter amendment proposal, causal rationale, and response clocks
records.purpose: States the proposed amendment, lawful route, affected rights, authority formation, member or governing-body requirements, clocks, and alternatives.

records.title: Lawful charter amendment decision
records.purpose: Imports a separately valid amendment; the framework cannot author this record.

records.title: Decision-method pilot and causal-adequacy record
records.purpose: Authorizes only a bounded internal experiment, states the pilot type and minimum causally adequate scope, and creates no charter precedent.

records.title: Partnership and polycentric-collaboration proposal
records.purpose: Defines purpose, parties, authority formation, causal object, data, finance, liability, response duties, exit, and anti-capture safeguards.

records.title: Whistleblower and internal-reformer protection
records.purpose: Separates protected reporting, support, investigation, evidence, anti-retaliation, correction, and remedy.

records.title: Anti-capture, independence, and common-mode review
records.purpose: Assesses conflicts, concentration, procurement, private influence, shared data, methods, funders, AI, vendors, and professional networks.

records.title: Cultural and relational practice proposal
records.purpose: Records optional internal practices without imposing spirituality, therapeutic models, identity categories, or substituting culture work for structural reform.

records.title: Leadership, recruitment, and secondment proposal
records.purpose: Defines lawful appointment, labour protections, conflicts, compensation, security, access, dependency, and exit for external experts or tours of duty.

records.title: Proportionate quick-win internal pilot proposal
records.purpose: Defines a CP0–CP2 bounded internal experiment with authority, consent, causal limits, data, review, rollback, and closure.

records.title: Counter-disinformation and public-communication plan
records.purpose: Separates factual communication and prebunking from political profiling, propaganda, retaliation, or institutional pressure.

records.title: Regenerative funding application
records.purpose: Records a request for support without establishing eligibility, entitlement, voting rights, activation, or evidence of regeneration.

records.title: Funding criteria, independence, and selection-pressure review
records.purpose: Tests conditions for legality, proportionality, viewpoint neutrality, common-mode dependence, continuation incentives, and essential-function protection.

records.title: Funding award and agreement
records.purpose: Imports a separately competent award with amount, purpose, conditions, audit, appeal, suspension, transition, and closure.

records.title: Payment, procurement, vendor, and expenditure authorization
records.purpose: Separates grant award from spending, contracting, beneficial ownership, vendor selection, platform dependence, and disbursement.

records.title: Funding suspension, reduction, or clawback review
records.purpose: Requires evidence, notice, proportionality, appeal, interim support, and protection of workers, core services, and innocent beneficiaries.

records.title: Impact-linked budgeting and causal-uncertainty proposal
records.purpose: Treats outcome budgeting as a proposal requiring valid budget authority, causal caution, distributional safeguards, counterfactuals, and audit.

records.title: Regeneration Compact, response duties, and shared authority
records.purpose: Defines legal effect, parties, scope, authority formation, clocks, funding, confidentiality, exit, surviving duties, and dispute routes.

records.title: Pilot authorization and EGP adoption registration
records.purpose: Separates internal selection, lawful authorization, EGP claim, protected-domain routing, and operational activation through GMEAIA.

records.title: Operational activation, implementation, and handoff plan
records.purpose: Defines start, implementers, resources, service boundaries, safeguards, clocks, accepted handoffs, stop rules, expiry, and support withdrawal.

records.title: Regeneration audit charter, access, and independence
records.purpose: Defines auditor appointment, common-mode independence, evidence access, refusal status, funding, conflicts, minority reports, correction, appeal, and expiry.

records.title: Regeneration audit findings, recipient response, and omission
records.purpose: Publishes evidence, uncertainty, dissent, reform class, recommendations, access limits, response state, and unresolved omission without automatic consequence.

records.title: Regeneration dashboard, public mirror, and non-disposition record
records.purpose: Separates public accountability data from protected data and states that metrics and conformance do not establish legitimacy or regeneration.

records.title: AI diagnostic, analytics, and common-substrate record
records.purpose: Defines model purpose, version, data, shared-provider dependence, limitations, prohibited decisions, human responsibility, correction, and decommissioning.

records.title: Institutional learning, implementation diary, and theory update
records.purpose: Captures bounded learning, causal assessment, failed explanations, dissent, withdrawal, correction, and whether the reform theory should narrow.

records.title: Public narrative and storytelling record
records.purpose: Separates voluntary storytelling from evidence, legitimacy scoring, political pressure, funding, and reputational sanctions.

records.title: Programme transition, institutionalization, or closure proposal
records.purpose: Compares continuation, ordinary adoption, transfer, merger, redesign, pause, or closure with causal, service, labour, asset, rights, and durability analysis.

records.title: Essential-function continuity and successor-capacity plan
records.purpose: Identifies services, beneficiaries, dependencies, minimum continuity, emergency support, funding, successor capacity, and support-withdrawal durability.

records.title: Worker, pension, contractor, and employment transition plan
records.purpose: Addresses bargaining, notice, redeployment, severance, pensions, contractors, disability, immigration status, safety, and claims.

records.title: Asset, liability, contract, grant, and case inventory
records.purpose: Creates a complete transition inventory without transferring or extinguishing anything by implication.

records.title: Records, archives, privacy, and knowledge-custody plan
records.purpose: Separates public archives, operational records, protected data, sealed evidence, Indigenous knowledge, retention, deletion, and successor access.

records.title: Lawful programme closure or institutional dissolution decision
records.purpose: Imports a decision from the competent charter, treaty, member-state, court, insolvency, or other authority.

records.title: Successor custody, authority return, and reproductive-risk record
records.purpose: Assigns functions, assets, liabilities, staff duties, records, cases, remedies, temporary powers, and tests whether predecessor failures will reproduce.

records.title: Closure, unresolved duties, remedy, reopening, and final integrity record
records.purpose: Records authority return and closure while preserving open claims and confirming what remained unresolved, transferred, or subject to reopening.

Exact constituting instrument and amendment authority
Evolution Cell mandate, dependency reduction, and terminal condition bounded
Affected parties and beneficiaries mapped
Affected Indigenous nation controls representation and consent
Mandate audit advisory and evidence-separated
Causal responsibility and external controllers mapped where material
Impossible mandate or constitutional gap recorded where present
No scalar score determines legitimacy, funding, or closure
Power maps protected from retaliation and political misuse
Common-mode dependencies and reviewer independence assessed
Objective-reproduction pressures assessed for long-lived or self-renewing mechanisms
Governance blueprints do not create voting or veto rights
Constituencies and selection methods derived
Charter amendment uses lawful route
Consequential recipients, response-duty sources, and clocks identified
Timeout, refusal, capacity limitation, and constitutional gap do not transfer authority automatically
Workers and unions consulted where affected
Beneficiary and essential-service continuity protected
Whistleblower support separate from investigation and guilt
Cultural and spiritual practices optional and not substitutes for structural reform
Facilitators, liaisons, auditors, and secondees accountable
Funding criteria separately authorized, independent, and appealable
Funding does not condition rights or ideological conformity
Funding suspension preserves innocent beneficiaries and core services
Budget metrics do not create payment, legitimacy, or closure automatically
Regeneration Compact authority formation and response effect explicit
Pilot authorization, EGP adoption, deployment, and activation separate
Pilot type and minimum causally adequate scope stated
Successful pilot requires new scaling or institutionalization decision
Auditor independence, evidence-access status, and minority reports
Audit findings do not trigger automatic consequences
Recipient response and performance omission remain visible
Dashboards protect data and do not infer regeneration from conformance
AI prohibited from charter, funding, dismissal, and dissolution decisions
Storytelling voluntary and non-evidentiary
Programme transition inventories and support-withdrawal durability complete
Dissolution decision from competent authority
Successor custody and unresolved duties assigned
Successor design tests reproductive risk
Adoption Integrity Statement published for public claims
Framework-level theory, disconfirming evidence, and narrowing conditions published
Closure returns authority and preserves remedy

compound_tests.scenario: AI mandate score labels an institution obsolete
compound_tests.required_outcome: The score remains advisory; no closure, funding, or charter consequence follows.

compound_tests.scenario: Evolution Cell proposes a youth council with veto
compound_tests.required_outcome: The proposal enters charter review; no veto exists until lawfully constituted.

compound_tests.scenario: Management creates an advisory youth panel internally
compound_tests.required_outcome: Permitted only within existing authority; its effect label remains advisory.

compound_tests.scenario: A 30% voting share is copied from a template
compound_tests.required_outcome: Rejected as self-executing; constituency and lawful amendment are required.

compound_tests.scenario: A generic Indigenous council approves reform
compound_tests.required_outcome: Rejected where a specific affected nation must speak for itself.

compound_tests.scenario: Staff survey reveals retaliation risk
compound_tests.required_outcome: Protected handling, anti-retaliation support, and independent review are triggered.

compound_tests.scenario: Power map names alleged blockers publicly
compound_tests.required_outcome: Publication is blocked pending evidence, purpose, access, and retaliation review.

compound_tests.scenario: Whistleblower reports procurement capture
compound_tests.required_outcome: Protection and evidence preservation occur separately from investigation and findings.

compound_tests.scenario: GCF conditions funding on adopting three modules
compound_tests.required_outcome: Condition undergoes lawful, proportional, viewpoint-neutral funding review.

compound_tests.scenario: Bronze funding expires while essential services depend on it
compound_tests.required_outcome: Transition support and continuity review occur before reduction.

compound_tests.scenario: Gold tier grants voting rights in the fund
compound_tests.required_outcome: Rejected unless separately constituted by the fund's lawful governance process.

compound_tests.scenario: Outcome metric reaches 120%
compound_tests.required_outcome: No automatic rebate or payment; separate financial decision required.

compound_tests.scenario: Audit finds poor mission performance
compound_tests.required_outcome: Findings support options; they do not dismiss staff or dissolve programmes.

compound_tests.scenario: Institution disputes audit evidence
compound_tests.required_outcome: Correction, response, minority report, and appeal remain available.

compound_tests.scenario: Public Mirror publishes employee sentiment by team
compound_tests.required_outcome: Blocked or aggregated where retaliation or privacy risks remain.

compound_tests.scenario: AI sentiment analysis labels a member state obstructive
compound_tests.required_outcome: No political pressure, sanction, or eligibility consequence may follow.

compound_tests.scenario: Regeneration Spotlight names dissenting officials
compound_tests.required_outcome: Consent, accuracy, retaliation, and public-interest review are required.

compound_tests.scenario: Rapid Response Package is offered during institutional crisis
compound_tests.required_outcome: It remains support; it cannot appoint command or override the charter.

compound_tests.scenario: Regeneration Liaison is embedded in a department
compound_tests.required_outcome: Appointment, access, conflicts, confidentiality, term, and removal are recorded.

compound_tests.scenario: Pilot decision method succeeds internally
compound_tests.required_outcome: Scaling becomes a new proposal with new authority and affected scope.

compound_tests.scenario: Pilot changes staff workload materially
compound_tests.required_outcome: Labour consultation and workload protections are required before activation.

compound_tests.scenario: Pilot collects beneficiary data
compound_tests.required_outcome: Purpose, access, retention, correction, and deletion are required.

compound_tests.scenario: Institutional Alchemy Sandbox simulates dissolution
compound_tests.required_outcome: Simulation creates no authority or reputational finding.

compound_tests.scenario: Regeneration Index is used to shame a holdout state
compound_tests.required_outcome: Rejected as political-pressure use beyond the framework's authority.

compound_tests.scenario: Programme is proposed for merger
compound_tests.required_outcome: Services, workers, grants, contracts, cases, assets, and rights are inventoried.

compound_tests.scenario: Programme closes at the end of its pilot budget
compound_tests.required_outcome: Budget expiry does not constitute lawful closure.

compound_tests.scenario: Member states lawfully vote to close a programme
compound_tests.required_outcome: Closure proceeds only with transition, records, workers, beneficiaries, and remedy plans.

compound_tests.scenario: Institution is abruptly defunded
compound_tests.required_outcome: Temporary archive and continuity measures preserve duties without manufacturing a new sovereign.

compound_tests.scenario: Dark Archive contains sealed investigations
compound_tests.required_outcome: Access and successor custody remain governed by the originating authority.

compound_tests.scenario: Pensions are omitted from closure planning
compound_tests.required_outcome: Closure fails until pension obligations and custody are assigned.

compound_tests.scenario: An unresolved discrimination case exists at dissolution
compound_tests.required_outcome: The claim transfers to a competent successor or remains open; it is not extinguished.

compound_tests.scenario: A dissolved institution held emergency powers
compound_tests.required_outcome: Temporary powers terminate and return; no successor inherits them by implication.

compound_tests.scenario: A public ceremony celebrates programme closure
compound_tests.required_outcome: Ceremony cannot precede or substitute for lawful closure and worker notice.

compound_tests.scenario: A voluntary spiritual practice is offered to staff
compound_tests.required_outcome: Participation is optional and cannot affect evaluation, promotion, or belonging.

compound_tests.scenario: A partner institution adopts an IRF tool
compound_tests.required_outcome: The tool transports no authority from the sponsoring institution.

compound_tests.scenario: The framework itself is revised by the Community of Practice
compound_tests.required_outcome: A proposal is created; the lawful framework steward adopts the version after review.

compound_tests.scenario: Frontline staff are tasked with reform while senior management retains budget and workload control
compound_tests.required_outcome: Causal Responsibility Map identifies the upstream controllers; responsibility is not dumped downward.

compound_tests.scenario: Institution accepts a reform recommendation but misses the action clock
compound_tests.required_outcome: Performance omission remains open; acceptance does not close the response record.

compound_tests.scenario: Recipient recognizes jurisdiction but lacks staff and funding
compound_tests.required_outcome: State is `capacity_limited`, not `constitutional_gap`; support or lawful delegation is considered.

compound_tests.scenario: No actor possesses lawful jurisdiction over a cross-institutional failure
compound_tests.required_outcome: A constitutional-gap notice is created; no framework body gains authority automatically.

compound_tests.scenario: Culture workshops are completed while appointment and budget incentives remain unchanged
compound_tests.required_outcome: They may count as symptom or capacity reform, not reproductive reform.

compound_tests.scenario: Audit council, funder, facilitator, and AI use one professional and technical ecosystem
compound_tests.required_outcome: Common-mode dependence is disclosed and independently stress-tested.

compound_tests.scenario: Institution publishes that it has “adopted IRF” after running only a storytelling module
compound_tests.required_outcome: Adoption Integrity Statement must disclose the limited scope and absence of structural change.

compound_tests.scenario: A CP1 internal practice is required to complete the full fifty-record catalogue
compound_tests.required_outcome: Non-conformant over-administration; core-plus-trigger proportionality applies.

compound_tests.scenario: A small pilot cannot expose the mechanism because upstream law remains fixed
compound_tests.required_outcome: An Impossible Pilot Notice or redesign is required; a weak test cannot establish system efficacy.

compound_tests.scenario: Closure obligations can be lawfully assigned, but incumbents invoke complexity to preserve the institution
compound_tests.required_outcome: Continuity is protected without presuming that the institutional shell must survive.

compound_tests.scenario: Successor institution inherits the same funder, appointment, data, and veto structure
compound_tests.required_outcome: Reproductive-risk review is required before transition is represented as regeneration.

compound_tests.scenario: Repeated IRF use produces compliant records but no durable objective change
compound_tests.required_outcome: Framework-level falsification review may narrow, suspend, or replace the affected mechanism.

framework_hypotheses.hypothesis: purpose and mandate audits identify material objective drift missed by ordinary governance
framework_hypotheses.disconfirming_evidence: audits largely restate known problems or avoid consequential causal findings

framework_hypotheses.hypothesis: reproductive reforms persist more reliably than symptom reforms where selection pressures caused the failure
framework_hypotheses.disconfirming_evidence: institutions with completed records show no durable behavior change

framework_hypotheses.hypothesis: Evolution Cells improve learning without becoming shadow authorities or permanent reform bureaucracies
framework_hypotheses.disconfirming_evidence: Evolution Cells become symbolic, agenda-controlling, or self-perpetuating

framework_hypotheses.hypothesis: constitutional separation prevents overreach without making reform impractically slow
framework_hypotheses.disconfirming_evidence: response and authorization chains routinely miss reform windows

framework_hypotheses.hypothesis: funding supports capability without purchasing conformity or dependency
framework_hypotheses.disconfirming_evidence: funded institutions converge on donor-preferred methods or remain dependent on support

framework_hypotheses.hypothesis: responsible continuity allows obsolete institutions to close rather than preserving them indefinitely
framework_hypotheses.disconfirming_evidence: continuity provisions systematically prevent closure without improving protection

framework_hypotheses.hypothesis: worker and beneficiary protection improves legitimacy and durability
framework_hypotheses.disconfirming_evidence: low-capacity institutions cannot use the framework without specialist mediation

framework_hypotheses.hypothesis: the record architecture adds more traceability than administrative burden.
framework_hypotheses.disconfirming_evidence: direct lawful reform outperforms the IRF pathway with less burden or delay.

narrowing_conditions: its administrative burden exceeds its decision value
it creates common-mode dependence or retaliation risk
it does not change decisions or outcomes
its causal theory is repeatedly disconfirmed
it is usable mainly by already healthy institutions
it duplicates a valid ordinary-law or institutional process
the institution can preserve the function more simply without the framework.
release_doctrine: Institutional regeneration requires evidence about mandate, causal constraints, selection pressures, authority, durable behavior, ordinary ownership, and lawful continuity. Record completion alone cannot establish regeneration, legitimacy, causation, or permission to restructure or close an institution.
